Game Night: five scene themes in Shoreline's spirit

Each theme is a living scene like Shoreline: a sky band the header floats on, a little world that moves (transform and opacity only), a matching palette and font, and its own procedural soundscape. Three are seasonal (Halloween, Christmas, 4th of July) and two suit a global audience (Diwali, and an evergreen rainforest). The phones are the app's real Home, Game picker and a Connect Four room at 390×844, scaled. In a game the scene shrinks to the header band so nothing moves near the board, which stays opaque. Turn on a theme's sound to hear it; only one plays at a time, the way the app plays one ambience. The volume slider sets that theme's level.

At a glance

Recommendation

Build Haunted Hollow now, then Winter Lights recommended

Halloween is three weeks away (window opens Oct 1, it is Oct 6 today), so Haunted Hollow is the only one that can ship inside its season this year. It upgrades the existing PUMPKIN NIGHT theme in place: same id and palette, so players who own the Seasonal pack get the scene for free. Winter Lights next, to land by Dec 1.

  • Festival of Lights is worth building this month too if India is a big share of players (the store already prices in INR). Diwali 2026 is Nov 8.
  • Stars & Stripes can wait until June. Its fireworks engine also covers New Year's Eve, so it is worth building once for both.
  • Monsoon Canopy is the evergreen pick: the calmest soundscape of the five and a light daytime partner for Shoreline.
  • Build the shared pieces first (half a day): a SCENES map in ThemeBackdrop instead of the beach-only check, an AMBIENCES entry per theme, and a seasonal date window in THEMES so Settings can offer the theme in season.

Your pick

For each theme: build it now, build it ahead of its season, or skip it. You can change the answers until you queue them.
